B_source.statement:
[[Wallis's Product]] can be written as:
:$\displaystyle \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \frac 1 {2 n + 1} \paren {\frac {2 \cdot 4 \cdots \paren {2 n} } {1 \cdot 3 \cdots \paren {2 n - 1} } }^2 = \frac \pi 2$

substitutions.the ratio of double factorials: 4^n divided by the central binomial coefficient

derived.the Wallis limit: the asymptotic size of C(2n, n)

object_map.reformulation: Recognize the Wallis ratio of even to odd double factorials as 4^n / C(2n, n).

validity_conditions: The identification uses 2 . 4 ... (2n) = 2^n n! and 1 . 3 ... (2n - 1) = (2n)! / (2^n n!).
The result also follows from Stirling's formula and gives the return probability of a random walk.
proof_plan:
We have $2 \cdot 4 \cdots \paren {2 n} = 2^n n!$ and $1 \cdot 3 \cdots \paren {2 n - 1} = \dfrac {\paren {2 n}!} {2^n n!}$.
Hence their ratio is $\dfrac {4^n \paren {n!}^2} {\paren {2 n}!} = \dfrac {4^n} {\dbinom {2 n} n}$.

By the source result:
:$\dfrac 1 {2 n + 1} \paren {\dfrac {4^n} {\dbinom {2 n} n} }^2 \to \dfrac \pi 2$
Hence $\dbinom {2 n} n^2 \sim \dfrac {2 \cdot 4^{2 n} } {\pi \paren {2 n + 1} } \sim \dfrac {4^{2 n} } {\pi n}$.

Taking square roots, $\dbinom {2 n} n \sim \dfrac {4^n} {\sqrt {\pi n} }$.
{{qed}}
